Growing literature proposes inference-time token reduction (FastV, VLA-IAP, H2O, ToMe). These methods succeed on some VLAs but their behavior across different architectures is unstudied.\\n\\n**Gap**: No work has systematically compared token pruning robustness across VLA architectures. The implicit assumption that \\\"token pruning works or fails uniformly\\\" is untested. The critical architectural factor determining prunability is unknown.\\n\\n**Discovery**: We find that VLA token pruning robustness is governed by two interacting axes. **Axis 1 — Token Coupling**: connector architecture determines whether tokens are independent (linear proj, MLP) or entangled (BART encoder, pixel-shuffle), diagnosed by importance CV (0.038→0.314). **Axis 2 — Task Complexity**: multi-step tasks (Goal/Long) amplify pruning damage on entangling connectors — X-VLA drops 27.8pp on Goal vs 1.6pp on Object at k=0.9. Evidence from 5 VLA models × 4 LIBERO suites:\\n- **Token-independent** (π0, π0.5 linear; OpenVLA, OFT MLP): graded degradation, CV 0.038–0.219\\n- **Token-entangling** (X-VLA BART 12L; SmolVLA pixel-shuffle): task-dependent collapse — tolerate simple tasks, catastrophic on complex tasks. CV 0.151–0.314\\nCV predicts both pruning tolerance and optimal strategy (L2norm hurts low-CV models, helps high-CV).\\n\\n**Solution**: Diagnose-then-Compress framework. Step 1: Token importance CV provides zero-cost diagnostic for pruning tolerance (one forward pass). Step 2: VTR (Vision Token Re-encoding) provides universal compression. For pixel-shuffle: recovers from 0% (hard pruning) to ~59% ≈ baseline (59.2%), M-curve flat (D105: M=16 56.9% ≈ M=128 58.0%, near-lossless at any compression ratio). For MLP projector: D109 C4-ext = 0% SR (overfitting at M=128); VTC-only M=32/M=64 in progress.\\n\\n**Headline result**: \\\"Across 5 VLA models (450M-7B) × 4 task suites, we find that token pruning robustness is governed by two axes: connector architecture (token-independent vs token-entangling, diagnosed by importance CV) and task complexity. Token-entangling connectors (BART encoder, pixel-shuffle) show dramatically amplified sensitivity under complex tasks — X-VLA drops 27.8pp on Goal vs 1.6pp on Object at the same keep ratio; SmolVLA collapses to 0% at 5% removal regardless of task. **Analysis contribution (primary)**: First systematic study revealing that VLA token pruning robustness is determined by the interaction of two axes: (1) connector architecture (token-independent vs token-entangling, diagnosed by importance CV 0.038→0.314) and (2) task complexity (simple vs multi-step). No competing work does cross-architecture, cross-task VLA token analysis.

**Method contribution**: Diagnose-then-Compress framework:
- Step 1: **Connector Compressibility Diagnostic** (D104: resolved)
  - **Primary metric: Importance CV** (token importance heterogeneity) — zero-cost, one forward pass
  - CV forms continuous spectrum predicting pruning tolerance: π0=0.038 < π0.5=0.055 < X-VLA=0.151 < OpenVLA=0.215 < OFT=0.219 < SmolVLA=0.314

**Differentiation from concurrent work**: 4 concurrent works (Compressor-VLA, SpecPrune-VLA, LightVLA ICRA'26, See What Matters ICML'26) all propose pruning on MLP-projector VLAs. We (1) explain why pruning fails on pixel-shuffle architectures, (2) identify why pruning succeeds on linear projection (tokens are truly independent), and (3) propose a re-encoding method motivated by the diagnostic analysis.

**Model coverage**: 5 VLA models × 3 connector families × 4 LIBERO suites × 4 model sizes (450M-7B). RC1 (only 2 models), RC2 (size confound), and RC7 (only one suite) fully addressed.

## Core Claims (5 claims, expanded from 4)

### Claim 1: 2-Axis Compressibility Framework (D107 → D171 UPGRADED)
Pruning sensitivity = f(connector_architecture, task_complexity). Two axes interact:

**Axis 1 — Token Coupling (connector determines base sensitivity):**
- **Token-independent** connectors (pure linear π0/π0.5, MLP OpenVLA/OFT): tokens retain spatial meaning → pruning damage is local, graded degradation
- **Token-entangling** connectors (BART X-VLA, pixel-shuffle SmolVLA): cross-token dependencies → pruning damage cascades

**Axis 2 — Task Complexity (task amplifies entangling-connector sensitivity):**
- Simple tasks (Object): even entangling connectors tolerate mild pruning (X-VLA k=0.9=97.6%)
- Complex tasks (Goal/Long): entangling connectors collapse (X-VLA Goal k=0.9=70.2%, Long k=0.95≈53%)
- Key: same connector, same k, same method — **only task differs** → 27.8pp drop (Object→Goal)

**CV predicts Axis-1 position**: 0.038 (most independent) → 0.055 → 0.151 → 0.215 → 0.219 → 0.314 (most entangled)

**Evidence**: 5 models, 3 connector families, 4 LIBERO suites, 4 model sizes (450M-7B). Key controlled comparisons:
1. π0 (256 tokens, linear) k=0.1 = 0.976 vs OpenVLA (256 tokens, MLP) k=0.1 = 1.608 → connector isolates base sensitivity
2. X-VLA Object k=0.9 = 97.6% vs X-VLA Goal k=0.9 = 70.2% → task complexity isolates amplification
3. SmolVLA Object = 0% at k=0.95 → extreme entanglement dominates even on simple tasks

🔴 **D108→D127→D130→D132: Pruning method comparison — MAJOR REVERSAL at aggressive compression**

Both L2 norm and random pruning tested on X-VLA and OpenVLA. **CV predicts not just tolerance but optimal strategy**:

- **OpenVLA (MLP, CV=0.215)**: L2 norm consistently ≥ random at all k values. High CV → meaningful importance differentiation → L2 norm selection effective.
  - k=0.95: L2norm=69.4% ≈ random=69.2% (+0.2pp)
  - k=0.7: L2norm=49.8%¹ > random=44.4% (+5.4pp). ¹seed43 only, seed42 running on westd-38929:2
  - k=0.5: L2norm=39.2% > random=35.8% (+3.4pp)
  - k=0.3: L2norm=25.0%, random=pending (re-running)

- **X-VLA (BART, CV=0.151)**: 🔴 **REVERSAL** — L2 norm ≈ random at mild compression, but **random MASSIVELY outperforms L2 norm at aggressive compression**:
  - k=0.9: L2norm=97.6% ≈ random=97.8% (≈0pp)
  - k=0.85: L2norm=68.0% > random=63.6% (+4.4pp, cliff boundary)
  - k=0.8: L2norm=89.0% ≈ random=89.4% (≈0pp, non-monotonic recovery)

  - k=0.7: L2norm=56.2% << random=65.2% (+9pp). Crossover confirmed at k≈0.8.

**KEY INSIGHT (D132→D137)**: Importance-based pruning can be **actively harmful** on low-CV architectures under aggressive compression, and the harm SCALES: +9pp@k=0.7, +28pp@k=0.5, +40pp@k=0.3. Mechanism: X-VLA's linear projection + BART encoder produces relatively uniform token norms (CV=0.151). L2 norm selection on a near-uniform distribution degenerates into selecting spatially clustered tokens → loses diversity → catastrophic failure. Random pruning preserves spatial coverage → dramatically better. Multi-seed confirmed.

**This strengthens the paper**: CV serves as a dual predictor — predicts both (1) pruning tolerance ceiling and (2) whether importance-based methods help or hurt. Connector architecture determines both via its effect on token importance distribution.

**Paper narrative upgrade**: From "connector determines compressibility" to "connector determines both compressibility AND optimal compression strategy." This is a significantly stronger and more novel contribution.

### Claim 2: Pixel Shuffle Creates Irreversible Token Entanglement
SmolVLA's pixel_shuffle connector spatially folds 1024 SigLIP patches into 64 tokens per camera (16x compression). Each resulting token encodes a 32x32 pixel region via channel-to-spatial reorganization. This creates extreme cross-token spatial entanglement: removing any single token eliminates an entire spatial quadrant's information with no redundancy to compensate.

**Evidence**:
- k=0.95 (remove only 7/128 tokens = 5.5%) = 0% SR — even minimal removal is catastrophic
- k=0.9 (remove 13/128 tokens) = 0% SR
- Geometric prior (Sobel edge) k=0.5/0.7/0.9 = all 0%
- Attention entropy ratio 0.952 (near-uniform, TV=0.05)
- Official checkpoint Object (59.2% baseline) cliff-edge at k=0.5 → 0%
- Official checkpoint Spatial (43.8% baseline) cliff-edge at k=0.5 → 0.6% (3/500, CI [0.2%, 1.7%])

**Problem**: Vision token efficiency is critical for real-time VLA deployment. Growing literature proposes inference-time token reduction (FastV, VLA-IAP, H2O, ToMe). These methods succeed on some VLAs but their behavior across different architectures is unstudied.

**Gap**: No work has systematically compared token pruning robustness across VLA architectures. The implicit assumption that "token pruning works or fails uniformly" is untested. The critical architectural factor determining prunability is unknown.

**Discovery**: We find that VLA token pruning robustness is governed by two interacting axes. **Axis 1 — Token Coupling**: connector architecture determines whether tokens are independent (linear proj, MLP) or entangled (BART encoder, pixel-shuffle), diagnosed by importance CV (0.038→0.314). **Axis 2 — Task Complexity**: multi-step tasks (Goal/Long) amplify pruning damage on entangling connectors — X-VLA drops 27.8pp on Goal vs 1.6pp on Object at k=0.9. **Headline result**: "Across 5 VLA models (450M-7B) × 4 task suites, we find that token pruning robustness is governed by two axes: connector architecture (token-independent vs token-entangling, diagnosed by importance CV) and task complexity. Token-entangling connectors (BART encoder, pixel-shuffle) show dramatically amplified sensitivity under complex tasks — X-VLA drops 27.8pp on Goal vs 1.6pp on Object at the same keep ratio; SmolVLA collapses to 0% at 5% removal regardless of task. Growing literature proposes inference-time token reduction (FastV, VLA-IAP, H2O, ToMe). These methods succeed on some VLAs but their behavior across different architectures is unstudied.\\n\\n**Gap**: No work has systematically compared token pruning robustness across VLA architectures. The implicit assumption that \\\"token pruning works or fails uniformly\\\" is untested. The critical architectural factor determining prunability is unknown.\\n\\n**Discovery**: We find that VLA token pruning robustness is governed by two interacting axes. **Axis 1 — Token Coupling**: connector architecture determines whether tokens are independent (linear proj, MLP) or entangled (BART encoder, pixel-shuffle), diagnosed by importance CV (0.038→0.314). **Axis 2 — Task Complexity**: multi-step tasks (Goal/Long) amplify pruning damage on entangling connectors — X-VLA drops 27.8pp on Goal vs 1.6pp on Object at k=0.9. Evidence from 5 VLA models × 4 LIBERO suites:\\n- **Token-independent** (π0, π0.5 linear; OpenVLA, OFT MLP): graded degradation, CV 0.038–0.219\\n- **Token-entangling** (X-VLA BART 12L; SmolVLA pixel-shuffle): task-dependent collapse — tolerate simple tasks, catastrophic on complex tasks. CV 0.151–0.314\\nCV predicts both pruning tolerance and optimal strategy (L2norm hurts low-CV models, helps high-CV).\\n\\n**Solution**: Diagnose-then-Compress framework. Step 1: Token importance CV provides zero-cost diagnostic for pruning tolerance (one forward pass). Step 2: VTR (Vision Token Re-encoding) provides universal compression. For pixel-shuffle: recovers from 0% (hard pruning) to ~59% ≈ baseline (59.2%), M-curve flat (D105: M=16 56.9% ≈ M=128 58.0%, near-lossless at any compression ratio). For MLP projector: D109 C4-ext = 0% SR (overfitting at M=128); VTC-only M=32/M=64 in progress.\\n\\n**Headline result**: \\\"Across 5 VLA models (450M-7B) × 4 task suites, we find that token pruning robustness is governed by two axes: connector architecture (token-independent vs token-entangling, diagnosed by importance CV) and task complexity. Token-entangling connectors (BART encoder, pixel-shuffle) show dramatically amplified sensitivity under complex tasks — X-VLA drops 27.8pp on Goal vs 1.6pp on Object at the same keep ratio; SmolVLA collapses to 0% at 5% removal regardless of task. CV (0.038→0.314) predicts both pruning tolerance and optimal strategy: importance-based pruning is actively harmful on low-CV architectures (+28-36pp gap favoring random), while it helps on high-CV models (+1-6pp). VTR recovers to ~59% (≈baseline) at any compression ratio (0-87.5%) where hard deletion achieves 0%.\\\"\\n\\n## Paper Structure (7-model version)\\n\\n1. **Introduction**: VLA efficiency motivation → diverse connector architectures → 2-axis framework discovery (D171) → Diagnose-then-Compress framework\\n2. **Background**: 5 VLA models, 3 connector families (linear/MLP/pixel-shuffle), 4 LIBERO suites, token flow analysis\\n3. **Experimental Setup**: 5 models, LIBERO benchmark (4 suites: Object/Spatial/Goal/Long), pruning protocol, VTR compression, diagnostic metrics\\n4. **Main Results**:\\n   - §4.1: 2-Axis Framework Overview (Table 1: 5 models × token coupling axis; Size is not the explanatory variable; connector type is.\\n\\n### RC3: Why not test SmolVLA without pixel_shuffle?\\n**Response**: SmolVLA's connector is integral (LLM expects 128 tokens, not 1024). Removing it requires retraining from scratch. OpenVLA comparison isolates the connector's role.\\n\\n### RC4: Smart compression — is re-encoding or compression the mechanism?\\n**Response (corrected with baseline=59.2%)**: VTR achieves near-lossless compression at any ratio — the M-curve is flat (M=16: 56.9% → M=128: 58.0%, all within ±3pp of baseline 59.2%). Two lines of evidence: (1) M=128 passthrough (58.0%) ≈ baseline (59.2%) — re-encoding recovers spatial entanglement to baseline level, not above it. (2) Architecture control: MLP adapter (63.4%) ≈ cross-attention (60.1%) with CI overlap — any re-encoding mechanism works. The key contribution is recovery from 0% (hard pruning) to ~59% (baseline), not exceeding baseline. Compression ratio is a free parameter with negligible SR cost.\\n\\n### RC5: Relationship to VLA-IAP\\n**Response**: VLA-IAP's 97.8% on OpenVLA is consistent with our finding: MLP projector preserves token independence. VLA-IAP untested on pixel_shuffle VLAs; our geometric prior experiments (0%) predict it would fail.\\n\\n### RC6: Is this just \\\"different models behave differently\\\"?\\n**Response**: We identify the specific mechanism (pixel_shuffle spatial folding) and provide evidence for WHY. Concrete design implications: future VLAs wanting efficiency should avoid pixel_shuffle or include learned re-encoding modules.\\n\\n### RC7: Only one benchmark (LIBERO-Object) → **ADDRESSING (D115, D119)**\\n**Response**: Expanded to ALL 4 LIBERO suites (Object/Spatial/Goal/Long) — 4 genuinely different task distributions (manipulation skills, spatial reasoning, goal-conditioned, long-horizon). Taxonomy consistency validated across suites. LIBERO-Plus robustness benchmark tested (D119) but abandoned: L1 camera perturbation collapses OpenVLA to SR=3.3% (consistent with leaderboard 0.8%), creating floor effect with no room for pruning analysis. This floor effect itself is noted in Discussion as evidence of general VLA brittleness under distribution shift. Sim-only limitation acknowledged.\\n\\n## All Experimental Evidence (confirmed)\\n\\n### SmolVLA Cliff-Edge\\n- Fine-tuned baseline (Object): 44.8% (224/500) — ⚠️ OLD reproduced checkpoint, superseded by official HF = 59.2%\\n- 6 pruning conditions (random/ACIS/ToMe × k=0.5/0.7/0.9): all 0%\\n- Geometric prior (Sobel) k=0.5/0.7/0.9: all 0%\\n- Attention entropy: 0.952 (flat, TV=0.05)\\n- Official checkpoint Object: 59.2% → 0% at k=0.5\\n- Official checkpoint Spatial: 43.8% → 0.6% (3/500, CI [0.2%, 1.7%]) at k=0.5 — near-zero, confirms cliff-edge across suites\\n- LoRA-FT checkpoint Spatial: 8.0% (per-task: [24,8,4,24,0,2,2,2,14,0]) — LoRA trained on Object only, does not transfer to Spatial. Use official checkpoint for cross-suite SmolVLA analysis.\\n\\n### OpenVLA Degradation Curve\\n- k=1.0: 74.0% (370/500)\\n- k=0.95: 69.4% (-6% relative)\\n- k=0.9: 62.0% (-16% relative)\\n- k=0.7: 49.0% (245/500, -34% relative)\\n- k=0.5: 37.4% (187/500, -49% relative)\\n- k=0.3: 20.6% (103/500, -72% relative)\\n- Entropy: 0.639 (progressive sharpening, TV=0.50)\\n\\n### Cross-Model Pruning Taxonomy (7 models — D100, D120, D127)\\n| Model | Connector | Tokens | k=0.1 norm_L1 | k=0.5 norm_L1 | Class |\\n|-------|-----------|--------|---------------|---------------|-------|\\n| π0 (3.3B) | Pure linear proj | 256 | 0.976 (-2.4%) | 0.983 | Immune |\\n| π0.5 (4B) | Pure linear proj (×√d scaling) | 768 (3×256) | **98.2%** (491/500) | **L2norm=33.4%, random=69.4%** | **Uniformly Critical (D139)**: L2norm catastrophic (-64.8pp), random tolerant (-28.8pp), gap=+36pp. CV=0.055. |\\n| X-VLA (880M) | Linear + BART 12L | 50 | ~1.00 | ~1.00 | Threshold-graded (k=0.7: 56.2%) |\\n| OpenVLA (7B) | 3-layer MLP | 256 | 1.608 (+61%) | 1.167 (+17%) | Smooth graded |\\n| OFT (7B) | 3-layer MLP (DINOv2+SigLIP fused) | **512** | N/A | N/A | D136: Blackwell GPU incompatible. CV=0.219≈OpenVLA → graded. Cite official ~97% baseline. |\\n| SmolVLA (450M) | Pixel-shuffle | 128 | — | 0% cliff | Catastrophic |\\n\\nDiagnostic metrics (D104+D106+D120: CV as continuous predictor, 7 models):\\n| Model | Connector (effective) | Entropy | CV | Pruning Behavior |\\n|-------|----------------------|---------|------|------------------|\\n| π0 | Pure linear proj | 0.959 | 0.038 | Immune (offline, k=0.1 improves) |\\n| π0.5 | Pure linear proj (×√d) | pending | 0.055 | **Uniformly Critical (D139)**: L2norm=33.4%, random=69.4%, gap=+36pp. Monotonic trend extreme. |\\n| X-VLA | Linear proj + BART enc (12L) | **0.614** | **0.151** | Threshold-graded: robust k≥0.9, cliff k=0.7 (56.2%). D127: random=L2norm at k=0.9 |\\n| OpenVLA | 3-layer MLP (GELU) | 0.661 | 0.215 | Graded (74→37.4% at k=0.5) |\\n| OFT | 3-layer MLP (DINOv2+SigLIP, **512 tokens**) | 0.667 | 0.219 | D136: Graded expected (CV≈OpenVLA). Blackwell GPU incompatible, no LIBERO SR. |\\n| SmolVLA | Pixel-shuffle (16×) | 0.952 | **0.314** | Catastrophic (0% at k=0.95) |\\n\\nKey insights (updated with 7-model data):\\n1. **CV is a continuous predictor**: 0.038 → 0.055 → 0.151 → 0.215 → 0.219 → 0.314 maps to decreasing pruning tolerance. NOT a 3-class discrete classifier.\\n2. **X-VLA CV=0.151 correctly predicted its intermediate behavior** — closer to OpenVLA (0.215) than π0 (0.038), matching k=0.7 SR ≈ OpenVLA k=0.7.\\n3. **X-VLA entropy=0.614 ≈ OpenVLA 0.661** — both have BART/MLP non-linear mixing. X-VLA is NOT \\\"high entropy\\\" like π0.\\n4. **Effective connector complexity matters more than nominal label**: X-VLA is \\\"linear proj\\\" but BART encoder introduces 12 transformer layers of mixing. Paper should discuss \\\"effective connector\\\" = projection + any intermediate processing.\\n5. OFT entropy 0.667 ≈ Standard 0.661 → action head does not affect attention structure\\n6. Framing: CV captures \\\"degree of non-linear mixing in the vision-to-LLM pathway.\\\" More mixing → higher CV → less tolerant of pruning.\\n\\n### Smart Compress (Learned Re-encoding)\\nCross-attention (VTC) M sweep (3-seed where available):\\n- M=16: **56.9% ± 1.3pp** (3-seed: 55.8/58.4/56.5) — 87.5% compression, ZERO loss vs M=128\\n- M=32: 60.1±1.3% (3-seed: 61.6/59.2/59.6)\\n- M=64: 62.0±2.3% (3-seed: 61.6/60.0/64.4)\\n- M=96: 54.5±3.2% (3-seed: 52.6/58.2/52.8) — highest variance\\n- M=128: 58.0±3.5pp (3-seed: 59.8/54.0/60.2) — passthrough control\\n- **D102 CONFIRMED: M-curve is flat.** M=16 (56.9%) = M=128 (58.0%), difference < 1.1pp. VTC achieves near-lossless compression at ANY ratio for pixel-shuffle connector. All M values within ±5pp of baseline ~59%.\\n\\nMLP adapter (M=32, 3-seed):\\n- seed42: 65.2% (326/500), seed43: 64.6% (323/500), seed44: 60.4% (302/500)\\n- Mean: 63.4% ± 2.6 vs VTC M=32 mean 60.1% ± 1.3\\n- t-test p≈0.15, no significant difference — confirms architecture-independence\\n\\n### D109: VTR on OpenVLA (MLP projector) — FAILED\\n- C4-ext M=128 at 20K steps: **0% SR** (0/44 episodes before eval termination)\\n- Failure mode: model outputs identical action every timestep (severe overfitting)\\n- Interpretation: VTR adds unnecessary complexity for MLP projector tokens (already individually meaningful). VTR specifically solves pixel-shuffle entanglement.\\n- VTC-only M=32 and M=64 training in progress on westd-41074:2-3\\n\\n### Cross-Suite VTR Generalization (SmolVLA)\\n- M=32 Spatial: 53.2% (vs official Spatial baseline 44.6% per ROADMAP, vs pruning 0.6% — recovery from cliff-edge, +8.6pp over baseline)\\n- M=32 Goal: 56.4% (vs official Goal baseline 60.8% per ROADMAP, vs pruning 0% — recovery from cliff-edge, -4.4pp below baseline)\\n- ⚠️ Cross-suite baselines need reconciliation: paper_framing previously used 43.8%/63.0%, ROADMAP uses 44.6%/60.8%. Use n=500 official checkpoint data as ground truth.\\n- Note: VTR trained on Object suite, evaluated cross-suite. Official baselines from different checkpoint (official vs LoRA-FT); comparisons should emphasize recovery from 0% rather than absolute performance vs uncompressed.\\n\\n### Pairwise Statistical Tests (Welch's t-test, n=3 per condition)\\n- M=32 VTC vs M=32 MLP: p=0.150 (not significant) — confirms architecture-independence\\n- M=64 VTC vs M=96 VTC: p=0.034 (significant) — M=96 dip confirmed real\\n- M=32 MLP vs M=96 VTC: p=0.022 (significant) — M=96 underperforms\\n- M=32/M=64/M=128 VTC cluster: all pairwise p>0.25 — robust across M values\\n- Bonferroni note: no pair survives correction at 10 tests; n=3 limits power (~0.2 for medium effects)\\n\\n### Supplementary\\n- Inference latency: 6% speedup at M=32\\n- KV-cache: 75% memory reduction at M=32\\n\", \"total_chars\": 51958, \"truncated\": false}, \"error\": null, \"metadata\": {}}"}

2	name: paper-writing-norms
3	description: 顶会级别论文写作风格规范——章节写法（Abstract/Intro/Related Work）、去 AI 风格、视觉密度、叙事哲学。Paper Agent 和 Worker 写论文章节时必须加载。
4	allowed-tools: [Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep]
5	scope: global
6	version: 2
7	priority: 9
8	tags:
9	  - writing

11	  - style

13	roles:
14	  - agent
15	  - worker
16	  - paper_agent
17	---
18	
19	# 论文写作风格规范
20	
21	> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。
22	
23	---
24	
25	## 一、总体写作哲学
26	
27	### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌
28	
29	- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
30	- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
31	- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
32	- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing
33	
34	### 1.2 主线统一性
35	
36	- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
37	- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
38	- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
39	- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线
40	
41	### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义
42	
43	- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
44	- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
45	- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
46	- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug
47	
48	### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文
49	
50	- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
51	- 重点学：
52	  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
53	  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
54	  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
55	  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
56	- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
57	- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文
58	
59	---
60	
61	## 二、Abstract 写作规范
62	
63	### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）
64	
65	Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
66	1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
67	2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
68	3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
69	4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献
70	
71	### 2.2 禁忌
72	
73	- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
74	- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
75	- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
76	- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
77	- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开
78	
79	### 2.3 审稿人视角检验
80	
81	写完后用这个标准自检：审稿人能否在 30 秒内判断——
82	- 问题是否重要？
83	- 方法是否清楚？
84	- 贡献是否可信？
85	- 结果是否有说服力？
86	
87	---
88	
89	## 三、Introduction 写作规范
90	
91	### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）
92	
93	Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：
94	
95	1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
96	2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
97	3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
98	4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
99	5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献
100	
101	### 3.2 整体叙事结构
102	
103	```
104	现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结
105	```
106	
107	### 3.3 禁忌
108	
109	- **禁止泛泛介绍**：不要开头就写 "LLMs have shown remarkable capabilities..."，要从具体问题切入
110	- **禁止缺少过渡**：每段之间必须有逻辑连接
111	- **禁止实验报告风格**：Introduction 不是 "我们做了 X 实验得到了 Y 结果" 的罗列
112	- 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
113	- Contribution 列表中不能出现未在前文铺垫过的概念
114	
115	---
116	
117	## 四、Related Work 写作规范
118	
119	### 4.1 目标
120	
121	让审稿人相信：作者理解这个领域，知道自己的方法站在什么位置，清楚相对已有工作的真实增量在哪里。
122	
123	### 4.2 结构要求
124	
125	- 把已有工作分成几个清晰的主题（如模型训练、推理增强、工具调用、数据构建、评测等）
126	- 每类简要说明：已有方法做了什么、解决了哪些问题、和本文的关系
127	- 帮助读者理解：哪些是本文直接继承的，哪些方法不同但解决相似问题，哪些留下了本文要解决的缺口
128	
129	### 4.3 禁忌
130	
131	- **禁止论文堆砌**：不要写成 "A proposed X. B proposed Y. C proposed Z." 的列表
132	- **目标不是展示读了多少论文**，而是做归纳和比较
133	- Contribution claim（"To our knowledge, no prior work..."）应放在 Introduction，不在 Related Work
134	
135	### 4.4 引用充足度
136	
137	- 引用必须覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**
138	- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
139	- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 五、去 AI 写作风格（硬规则）
144	
145	以下模式是 AI 生成文本的典型标志，审稿人一眼能看出。**必须全部消除。**
146	
147	### 5.1 严禁破折号（最显著的 AI 痕迹）
148	
149	**这是 AI 写作最容易被识别的标志，审稿人最敏感。单列为最高优先级硬规则。**
150	
151	- 解释性 em-dash（—，U+2014）和 en-dash（–，U+2013）必须**全部删除**
152	- 替代方式：用逗号、括号或拆分为两个句子
153	- 强制检查命令：
154	  ```bash
155	  grep -n "—" paper/*.tex     # em-dash，每处人工判断是否必要
156	  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
157	  ```
158	- 例外（允许保留）：表格分隔符、数字范围（`2020–2024`、`pp. 12–18`）、专有名词（`Newton–Raphson`）
159	
160	### 5.2 段落与句式
161	
162	- **禁止过度分段**：不需要每 2-3 句就换段，自然段 5-8 句是正常的
163	- **减少关系从句**（which, that, who）：能用简洁直接的句子就不用从句
164	- **禁止 -ing 短语结尾**：如 "..., highlighting the applicability of..." / "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."。这是 AI 写作最典型的标志之一
165	- **禁止连续使用 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"**：一段内最多用一个过渡词
166	- **避免 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."**：直接写要说的内容
167	
168	### 5.3 用词黑名单
169	
170	- 避免 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "facilitate" — 用 "explore" / "use" / "enable"
171	- 避免 "a myriad of" / "a plethora of" — 用 "many" / "various"
172	- 避免 "in the realm of" / "in the context of" — 直接说
173	- 避免 "paradigm shift" / "novel" 过度使用
174	
175	### 5.4 校对清单（4 步）
176	
177	1. 全文 proofread 语法和拼写
178	2. 检查所有代词/指示词（this, that, it）是否指代明确
179	3. **`grep "—"` + `grep " – "` 全文清零**（删除所有解释性 dash，§5.1）
180	4. `grep "ing,"` 模式——大部分 -ing 分词短语需要改写
181	
182	---
183	
184	## 六、图表与视觉规范
185	
186	### 6.1 知识密度原则
187	
188	- **图表的信息必须紧凑**——不能为了美观而留大量白空间
189	- 一张图如果只传达一个简单信息，要么缩小要么合并到其他图中
190	- 能用 inline text 说清的不要占一整个 Figure
191	
192	### 6.2 表格规范
193	
194	- 表格和正文文字不能视觉重叠（检查 column 宽度和 alignment）
195	- 小数精度全表统一
196	- 最优加粗、次优下划线
197	- Caption 必须自包含
198	
199	### 6.3 图片规范
200	
201	- 数值标签不能被线、bar、点遮住——用白色背景或偏移标签
202	- 图中字体 >= 7pt（打印后仍可读）
203	- 栏宽约束需匹配目标 venue 模板要求
204	- 概念图/流程图要有信息量，不要画一个 trivial 的 pipeline 然后占半页
205	
206	### 6.4 空间效率
207	
208	- 顶会正文页数严格受限（具体页数查目标会议官网），每 cm² 都是宝贵资源
209	- 优先使用 `\subfigure` 合并相关图
210	- Table 能 inline 就不要单独浮动
211	- 图表占比与其对叙事的贡献成正比
212	
213	### 6.5 页面节奏
214	
215	好论文的页面有节奏感——text、equation、figure 交替出现，读者视觉不疲劳：
216	
217	- **text-equation-figure 三重奏**：重要概念用"文字解释 → 公式定义 → 图表直觉"三步展开
218	- 连续 2 页纯文本（无 figure/equation/table）→ 穿插一个 display item 打破节奏
219	- 连续 2 个 figure 页（整页被 float 占满）→ 至少隔 1 段文字再放下一个 float
220	- Section heading 不孤悬页底（heading 后至少跟 2 行正文，否则强制分页）

# 论文写作风格规范

> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。

---

## 一、总体写作哲学

### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌

- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing

### 1.2 主线统一性

- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线

### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义

- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug

### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文

- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
- 重点学：
  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文

---

## 二、Abstract 写作规范

### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）

Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献

### 2.2 禁忌

- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开

### 2.3 审稿人视角检验

写完后用这个标准自检：审稿人能否在 30 秒内判断——
- 问题是否重要？
- 方法是否清楚？
- 贡献是否可信？
- 结果是否有说服力？

---

## 三、Introduction 写作规范

### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）

Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：

1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献

### 3.2 整体叙事结构

```
现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结
```

### 3.3 禁忌

- **禁止泛泛介绍**：不要开头就写 "LLMs have shown remarkable capabilities..."，要从具体问题切入
- **禁止缺少过渡**：每段之间必须有逻辑连接
- **禁止实验报告风格**：Introduction 不是 "我们做了 X 实验得到了 Y 结果" 的罗列
- 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
- Contribution 列表中不能出现未在前文铺垫过的概念

---

## 四、Related Work 写作规范

### 4.1 目标

让审稿人相信：作者理解这个领域，知道自己的方法站在什么位置，清楚相对已有工作的真实增量在哪里。

### 4.2 结构要求

- 把已有工作分成几个清晰的主题（如模型训练、推理增强、工具调用、数据构建、评测等）
- 每类简要说明：已有方法做了什么、解决了哪些问题、和本文的关系
- 帮助读者理解：哪些是本文直接继承的，哪些方法不同但解决相似问题，哪些留下了本文要解决的缺口

### 4.3 禁忌

- **禁止论文堆砌**：不要写成 "A proposed X. B proposed Y. C proposed Z." 的列表
- **目标不是展示读了多少论文**，而是做归纳和比较
- Contribution claim（"To our knowledge, no prior work..."）应放在 Introduction，不在 Related Work

### 4.4 引用充足度

- 引用必须覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**
- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足

---

## 五、去 AI 写作风格（硬规则）

以下模式是 AI 生成文本的典型标志，审稿人一眼能看出。**必须全部消除。**

### 5.1 严禁破折号（最显著的 AI 痕迹）

**这是 AI 写作最容易被识别的标志，审稿人最敏感。单列为最高优先级硬规则。**

- 解释性 em-dash（—，U+2014）和 en-dash（–，U+2013）必须**全部删除**
- 替代方式：用逗号、括号或拆分为两个句子
- 强制检查命令：
  ```bash
  grep -n "—" paper/*.tex     # em-dash，每处人工判断是否必要
  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
  ```
- 例外（允许保留）：表格分隔符、数字范围（`2020–2024`、`pp. 12–18`）、专有名词（`Newton–Raphson`）

### 5.2 段落与句式

- **禁止过度分段**：不需要每 2-3 句就换段，自然段 5-8 句是正常的
- **减少关系从句**（which, that, who）：能用简洁直接的句子就不用从句
- **禁止 -ing 短语结尾**：如 "..., highlighting the applicability of..." / "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."。这是 AI 写作最典型的标志之一
- **禁止连续使用 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"**：一段内最多用一个过渡词
- **避免 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."**：直接写要说的内容

### 5.3 用词黑名单

- 避免 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "facilitate" — 用 "explore" / "use" / "enable"
- 避免 "a myriad of" / "a plethora of" — 用 "many" / "various"
- 避免 "in the realm of" / "in the context of" — 直接说
- 避免 "paradigm shift" / "novel" 过度使用

### 5.4 校对清单（4 步）

1. 全文 proofread 语法和拼写
2. 检查所有代词/指示词（this, that, it）是否指代明确
3. **`grep "—"` + `grep " – "` 全文清零**（删除所有解释性 dash，§5.1）
4. `grep "ing,"` 模式——大部分 -ing 分词短语需要改写

---

## 六、图表与视觉规范

### 6.1 知识密度原则

- **图表的信息必须紧凑**——不能为了美观而留大量白空间
- 一张图如果只传达一个简单信息，要么缩小要么合并到其他图中
- 能用 inline text 说清的不要占一整个 Figure

### 6.2 表格规范

- 表格和正文文字不能视觉重叠（检查 column 宽度和 alignment）
- 小数精度全表统一
- 最优加粗、次优下划线
- Caption 必须自包含

### 6.3 图片规范

- 数值标签不能被线、bar、点遮住——用白色背景或偏移标签
- 图中字体 >= 7pt（打印后仍可读）
- 栏宽约束需匹配目标 venue 模板要求
- 概念图/流程图要有信息量，不要画一个 trivial 的 pipeline 然后占半页

### 6.4 空间效率

- 顶会正文页数严格受限（具体页数查目标会议官网），每 cm² 都是宝贵资源
- 优先使用 `\subfigure` 合并相关图
- Table 能 inline 就不要单独浮动
- 图表占比与其对叙事的贡献成正比

### 6.5 页面节奏

好论文的页面有节奏感——text、equation、figure 交替出现，读者视觉不疲劳：

- **text-equation-figure 三重奏**：重要概念用"文字解释 → 公式定义 → 图表直觉"三步展开
- 连续 2 页纯文本（无 figure/equation/table）→ 穿插一个 display item 打破节奏
- 连续 2 个 figure 页（整页被 float 占满）→ 至少隔 1 段文字再放下一个 float
- Section heading 不孤悬页底（heading 后至少跟 2 行正文，否则强制分页）
- 最后一页内容 ≥ 2/3 页面高度（太空显得凑数，太满放不下 references）

### 6.6 表格 LaTeX 规范

**Booktabs 标准（硬规则）**：
- 用 `\toprule` / `\midrule` / `\bottomrule`，禁止 `\hline`，禁止竖线 `|`
- 用 `\centering` 不用 `\begin{center}`（后者多加垂直空白）
- 最优结果加粗（`\textbf{}`），次优下划线（`\underline{}`）+ 方向箭头 `↑`/`↓` 标明指标方向
- 小数精度全表统一（如全部保留 1 位或 2 位）
- Caption 在表格上方（`\caption` 在 `\begin{tabular}` 之前）

**宽度决策树**：
- ≤5 列 → 单栏宽度（`\columnwidth`）
- 6–8 列 → 全文宽度（`\textwidth`，双栏模板用 `table*`）
- >8 列 → 拆成两张表或移入 appendix

---

## 七、投稿前通用准备

### 7.1 模板必须官方（硬规则）

- LaTeX 模板**必须从目标会议官网下载**（CallForPapers / Author Instructions 页面）
- **不要用**：
  - 网上他人转载的复制版本（可能被改过 margin / 行号设置）
  - 上一年的模板（参数可能变：字体、margin、行号、anonymous 选项等）
  - 组里学长留的旧版本（来源不明、无法追溯）
- 风险：
  - 样式不符合 → desk reject
  - margin 不对 → 被审稿人质疑诚信
  - reference 格式错 → 被认为不规范
- 流程：先查会议官网 templates → 找不到再 `WebSearch "{venue} {year} latex template official"` → 仍找不到汇报 Director（不要用就近年版本顶替）
- `\documentclass[]{}` 选项必须与目标 venue + 阶段（review / camera-ready）一致

### 7.2 投稿要求逐项核对

- 目标会议如要求 Checklist / Ethical Statement / Broader Impact Statement / Reproducibility Statement，必须**认真填每一项**，不要全写 N/A
- 页数限制：查目标会议官网
- 匿名化要求：review 版 vs camera-ready 版本设置不同
- 行号开启（review 版常需）
- 字体大小、margin 不得修改 sty 文件

### 7.3 最终修改 10 项检查流程

提交前必须逐一检查：
1. 所有最新实验结果已全部录入
2. 根据实验结果将叙事调至最优状态
3. 附录所有内容在正文中被引用且融入叙事
4. 无数据堆砌（每个数字服务于叙事推进）
5. Abstract 和 Introduction 具有吸引力（不是实验报告风格）
6. 全文主线统一（idea 变化后各章节逻辑一致）
7. 所有专有名词有定义
8. 无 AI 风格标志（dash、-ing phrases、过度分段）
9. 图表知识密度高、无视觉遮挡
10. Reference 覆盖直接相关方法、baseline、benchmark、理论基础

\paragraph{Benchmark.} We evaluate on LIBERO~\cite{liu2023libero}, a simulated tabletop manipulation benchmark comprising four task suites of increasing complexity. \textbf{Object} (10 tasks) requires discriminating among visually similar objects at identical locations. \textbf{Spatial} (10 tasks) requires understanding relative spatial layouts (e.g., ``pick the bowl on the left of the plate''), where critical information is distributed across the visual field. \textbf{Goal} (10 tasks) involves goal-conditioned manipulation with varied target configurations. \textbf{Long} (10 tasks) chains 3--5 manipulation primitives into multi-step sequences, where token loss at any step can cascade through the remainder of the trajectory. Each task provides 50 demonstration episodes for fine-tuning and 50 evaluation episodes, yielding 500 episodes per suite.

\paragraph{Models.} Four VLAs are evaluated in closed-loop control: $\pi_{0.5}$~\cite{black2025pi05} (4B, linear projection, 768 tokens, CV$\,{=}\,$0.055), X-VLA~\cite{zheng2025xvla} (0.9B, linear + 12-layer BART encoder, 50 tokens, CV$\,{=}\,$0.151), OpenVLA~\cite{kim2024openvla} (7B, 3-layer MLP, 256 tokens, CV$\,{=}\,$0.215), and SmolVLA~\cite{shukor2025smolvla} (450M, pixel-shuffle $4{\times}4$, 128 tokens, CV$\,{=}\,$0.314). Two additional models ($\pi_{0}$~\cite{black2024pi0}, OFT~\cite{kim2025openoft}) contribute to the CV diagnostic via offline metrics only. Table~\ref{tab:model_properties} summarizes all six architectures.

\paragraph{Protocol.} We prune at $k \in \{0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.85, 0.9, 0.95\}$ and report mean success rate (SR) over 500 episodes in strict evaluation mode (episodes run to completion regardless of intermediate failures). Multi-seed results ($\pi_{0.5}$ Long: five seeds, 42--46; VTR: three seeds, 42--44) report mean $\pm$ standard deviation with per-seed breakdowns in the appendix. Single-seed results report Wilson 95\% confidence intervals.

\paragraph{Benchmark.} We evaluate on LIBERO~\cite{liu2023libero}, a simulated tabletop manipulation benchmark comprising four task suites of increasing complexity. \textbf{Object} (10 tasks) requires discriminating among visually similar objects at identical locations. \textbf{Spatial} (10 tasks) requires understanding relative spatial layouts (e.g., ``pick the bowl on the left of the plate''), where critical information is distributed across the visual field. \textbf{Goal} (10 tasks) involves goal-conditioned manipulation with varied target configurations. \textbf{Long} (10 tasks) chains 3--5 manipulation primitives into multi-step sequences, where token loss at any step can cascade through the remainder of the trajectory. Each task provides 50 demonstration episodes for fine-tuning and 50 evaluation episodes, yielding 500 episodes per suite.

\paragraph{Models.} Four VLAs are evaluated in closed-loop control: $\pi_{0.5}$~\cite{black2025pi05} (4B, linear projection, 768 tokens, CV$\,{=}\,$0.055), X-VLA~\cite{zheng2025xvla} (0.9B, linear + 12-layer BART encoder, 50 tokens, CV$\,{=}\,$0.151), OpenVLA~\cite{kim2024openvla} (7B, 3-layer MLP, 256 tokens, CV$\,{=}\,$0.215), and SmolVLA~\cite{shukor2025smolvla} (450M, pixel-shuffle $4{\times}4$, 128 tokens, CV$\,{=}\,$0.314). Two additional models ($\pi_{0}$~\cite{black2024pi0}, OFT~\cite{kim2025openoft}) contribute to the CV diagnostic via offline metrics only. Table~\ref{tab:model_properties} summarizes all six architectures.

\paragraph{Protocol.} We prune at $k \in \{0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.75, 0.85, 0.9, 0.95\}$ and report mean success rate (SR) over 500 episodes in strict evaluation mode (episodes run to completion regardless of intermediate failures). Multi-seed results ($\pi_{0.5}$ Long: five seeds, 42--46; VTR: three seeds, 42--44) report mean $\pm$ standard deviation with per-seed breakdowns in the appendix. Single-seed results report Wilson 95\% confidence intervals.

lines: \subsection{Experimental Setup}
\label{sec:exp_setup}

-We evaluate vision token pruning across six VLA architectures spanning three connector families on LIBERO~\cite{liu2023libero}, which provides four task suites of increasing complexity: Object, Spatial, Goal, and Long (10 tasks $\times$ 50 episodes each).

+\paragraph{Benchmark.} We evaluate on LIBERO~\cite{liu2023libero}, a simulated tabletop manipulation benchmark comprising four task suites of increasing complexity. \textbf{Object} (10 tasks) requires discriminating among visually similar objects at identical locations. \textbf{Spatial} (10 tasks) requires understanding relative spatial layouts (e.g., ``pick the bowl on the left of the plate''), where critical information is distributed across the visual field. \textbf{Goal} (10 tasks) involves goal-conditioned manipulation with varied target configurations. \textbf{Long} (10 tasks) chains 3--5 manipulation primitives into multi-step sequences, where token loss at any step can cascade through the remainder of the trajectory. Each task provides 50 demonstration episodes for fine-tuning and 50 evaluation episodes, yielding 500 episodes per suite.

-Four models are evaluated in closed-loop control: $\pi_{0.5}$~\cite{black2025pi05} (4B, linear projection, 768 tokens, CV$\,{=}\,$0.055), X-VLA~\cite{zheng2025xvla} (0.9B, linear + 12-layer BART encoder, 50 tokens, CV$\,{=}\,$0.151), OpenVLA~\cite{kim2024openvla} (7B, 3-layer MLP, 256 tokens, CV$\,{=}\,$0.215), and SmolVLA~\cite{shukor2025smolvla} (450M, pixel-shuffle $4{\times}4$, 128 tokens, CV$\,{=}\,$0.314). Two additional models ($\pi_{0}$~\cite{black2024pi0}, OFT~\cite{kim2025openoft}) are analyzed via offline metrics only. Table~\ref{tab:model_properties} summarizes all six architectures. We prune at $k \in \{0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.75, 0.85, 0.9, 0.95\}$, reporting mean success rate (SR) over 500 episodes.

+\paragraph{Models.} Four VLAs are evaluated in closed-loop control: $\pi_{0.5}$~\cite{black2025pi05} (4B, linear projection, 768 tokens, CV$\,{=}\,$0.055), X-VLA~\cite{zheng2025xvla} (0.9B, linear + 12-layer BART encoder, 50 tokens, CV$\,{=}\,$0.151), OpenVLA~\cite{kim2024openvla} (7B, 3-layer MLP, 256 tokens, CV$\,{=}\,$0.215), and SmolVLA~\cite{shukor2025smolvla} (450M, pixel-shuffle $4{\times}4$, 128 tokens, CV$\,{=}\,$0.314). Two additional models ($\pi_{0}$~\cite{black2024pi0}, OFT~\cite{kim2025openoft}) contribute to the CV diagnostic via offline metrics only. Table~\ref{tab:model_properties} summarizes all six architectures.

Multi-seed results ($\pi_{0.5}$ Long: five seeds, 42--46; VTR: three seeds, 42--44) report mean $\pm$ standard deviation with per-seed breakdowns in the appendix. Single-seed results report Wilson 95\% confidence intervals.
\subsection{Two-Axis Framework Overview}
\label{sec:two_axis}

Three qualitatively distinct response patterns emerge across the connector spectrum (Table~\ref{tab:main_results}; Figure~\ref{fig:pruning_overview}); a fourth (OpenVLA, MLP connector) is detailed in Appendix Table~\ref{tab:full_results}.

-\textbf{$\pi_{0.5}$ (linear, CV$\,{=}\,$0.055).} Low-CV models are \emph{uniformly critical}: which tokens are removed matters more than how many. L2 maintains ${\geq}$98.0\% through $k{=}0.85$, while random at $k{=}0.9$ collapses to 9.0\%---an 89\,pp method gap from identical removal fractions.

+\textbf{$\pi_{0.5}$ (linear, CV$\,{=}\,$0.055).} Low-CV models are \emph{uniformly critical}: which tokens are removed matters more than how many. On Object, L2 maintains ${\geq}$98.0\% through $k{=}0.85$ (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:full_results}), while random at $k{=}0.9$ collapses to 9.0\%, an 89\,pp method gap from identical removal fractions.

\textbf{X-VLA (BART encoder, CV$\,{=}\,$0.151).} Method-insensitive but task-sensitive: at $k{=}0.9$ on Object, L2 and random differ by 0.4\,pp, yet the same model drops 27.4\,pp on Goal. Removing 3 of 50 tokens ($k{=}0.95$) halves Long SR regardless of method.

\textbf{OpenVLA (MLP, CV$\,{=}\,$0.215).} OpenVLA exhibits scoring crossover: L2 outperforms random on Object but the ranking inverts on Spatial and Goal at $k{=}0.9$ (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:full_results}; Section~\ref{sec:analysis}).
-\textbf{SmolVLA (pixel-shuffle, CV$\,{=}\,$0.314).} Removing 6 of 128 tokens ($k{=}0.95$) collapses SR to ${\leq}$6.6\% across all suites and methods---a catastrophic cliff detailed below.

+\textbf{SmolVLA (pixel-shuffle, CV$\,{=}\,$0.314).} Removing 6 of 128 tokens ($k{=}0.95$) collapses SR to ${\leq}$6.6\% across all suites and methods, a catastrophic cliff detailed in Section~\ref{sec:pixel_shuffle}.

\label{sec:zeromask}
